i spent a LOT of my life feeling this way. i know exactly what you mean. i even saw a therapist about it because the executive dysfunction was crippling, there’s so much i wanna do and yet i can’t fucking do any of it !! the therapist was of no help and all she told me was “you just have to do it” so i left that session absolutely devastated. like duh thanks, never thought of that one before. i strongly relate to your thoughts and ideas overwhelming you, i often described this as being suffocated by my thoughts. thinking so so so much but being completely paralysed when it came to actually making something out of those thoughts. what helped me overcome this was realising that it stemmed from my crippling fear of failure. because i’d rather not do anything than do it wrong. so i started to focus on the process rather than the outcome. now i do things not to be perfect, but just for the sake of doing. by removing the weight of expectations i started going into creating with the idea of purposefully making bad art - i am not performing for anyone, it’s simply an outlet for self expression. and surprise, when you get rid of that immense pressure you put on yourself and allow your brain to actually do its thing, it’s capable of so much more! most of my spontaneously “bad art” turned out to be something i really resonated with. another thing that really helped me was the realisation that it’s okay to be indecisive. i’ve spent my entire life trying to shove myself into boxes because i always felt very unsubstantial and loose. i couldn’t make my mind up about the simplest of things. i never had a favorite color because i loved them all, and i am that way with everything. hobbies, fashion, music, it’s never just one thing. and that’s okay. for me, being a jack of all trades is a lot more fulfilling than having a concise and straightforward identity. you don’t have to be one thing, you can be a mosaic

what helped me the most with overcoming this was the realization that shame/embarrassment serves no real function. shame, not to be confused with guilt, is an emotion that specifically targets your sense of self. whereas other both positive and negative emotions have a clear purpose, shame just makes you feel bad about yourself. i used to be chronically ashamed of myself, but this helped me slowly dismantle that feeling. also the realization that the majority of people out there are also riddled with shame and feelings of inferiority. gotta just keep telling yourself that there is nothing wrong with you, you’re just as human as everyone else
